Interactive Census Variables Explorer

Source: R/sus_census_explore.R
sus_census_select.Rd

Lists the Brazilian Census variables (code, label, dataset, category) that can be requested from sus_census_join(), either in an interactive HTML page, as a console summary, or as a character vector of codes. Use it before sus_census_join() to choose census_vars. It does not need or change any climasus_df.

Usage

sus_census_select(
  dataset = "all",
  year = 2010,
  lang = "pt",
  output = "browser",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

dataset

Character scalar, one of "all" (default; the five microdata datasets), "population", "households", "families", "mortality", "emigration", "tracts" (see Details: currently unsupported). Other values error.

year

Numeric scalar, 2010 (default) or 2000 (2022 is not accepted here; other values error). Only labels the output.

lang

Character scalar. Language of variable labels and messages: "pt" (default), "en" or "es"; other values error.

output

Character scalar. "browser" (default) opens an interactive HTML page (temporary file) and returns the table invisibly; "console" prints a summary per dataset and returns the table invisibly; "codes" returns the unique variable codes. Other values error.

verbose

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), prints informative messages (for output = "codes" also a short preview).

Value

Depending on output:

  • "browser" and "console": invisibly, a data.frame with columns code, name, dataset, type ("regular_variable" or "imputation_marker"), category, has_categories, n_categories and year.

  • "codes": a character vector of unique variable codes, to pass to census_vars in sus_census_join().

Details

Variables come from the package's bundled dictionaries (population, households, families, mortality, emigration), in the requested lang. The dictionaries do not depend on year, which only labels the output. Codes starting with "M" are flagged as imputation markers. The "tracts" value is accepted by validation but no tract dictionary is bundled, so dataset = "tracts" currently errors ("No variables found"); for tract tables see censobr::read_tracts() and the tracts_dataset argument of sus_census_join(). With dataset = "all" only the five microdata datasets are listed.

See also

sus_census_join(), sus_socio_compute_indicators()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Open interactive explorer for all datasets
sus_census_select()

# Explore only population variables in the console
sus_census_select(dataset = "population", output = "console")

# Get variable codes for programmatic use
vars <- sus_census_select(
  dataset = "population",
  output = "codes",
  lang = "en"
)

# Use them in sus_census_join() (df: climasus_df at stage "spatial")
data <- sus_census_join(
  df = my_data,
  census_vars = vars[1:2],
  dataset = "population",
  year = 2010
)
} # }
